title: Grouping
explanation: Partition into groups: precompute the score of every subset, then dp[mask] over submasks. Enumerating all submasks of all masks is 3^16 ≈ 4.3e7.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[mask] = best total score for splitting exactly the rabbits in mask into groups
dp[i][g] = best score placing the first i rabbits, rabbit i in group g
options.why: Group scores depend on all members, not just the newest one.

options.text: dp[mask][k] = best score using k groups
options.why: The number of groups is free; the extra dimension doesn't help.

options.text: dp[i] = best score for the first i rabbits
options.why: Groups aren't contiguous in index order.

extraLayers.explanation: N ≤ 16 and 'partition into groups' → submask DP on the set of rabbits already grouped.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[mask] = max over non-empty submasks s ⊆ mask of score[s] + dp[mask \ s]
dp[mask] = max over i ∈ mask of dp[mask \ {i}] + score[{i}]
options.why: Only ever forms groups of size 1.

options.text: dp[mask] = Σ over submasks s of dp[s]
options.why: Sum, not max, and it double-counts.

extraLayers.explanation: Choose the group that will be formed last (a submask), add its precomputed score. Fixing its lowest bit avoids counting each partition many times.
